short: Queen at six days old, deposed at twenty-four, executed at forty-four.
full:
Mary became Queen of Scots when her father James V died six days after her birth in December 1542. Raised in France and married to the dauphin, she was briefly queen consort there before returning in 1561 to a Scotland that had turned Protestant in her absence, a Catholic widow of eighteen.

Her personal rule lasted six years. Her marriage to Lord Darnley produced a son, the future James VI, and then a murder: Darnley was killed at Kirk o' Field in February 1567, and Mary's marriage three months later to the Earl of Bothwell, widely suspected of the killing, destroyed her remaining support. Defeated at Carberry Hill, she was forced to abdicate in July 1567 and fled to England the following year. Elizabeth I held her for nineteen years as the focus of Catholic plotting, and after the Babington Plot had her tried and beheaded at Fotheringhay in February 1587.
